raw_response:
I’m already 62, and with only 12 mu and 2 people in the house, I can’t spread myself too thin. Cotton is still my main cash crop, so I’ll keep most of the land in cotton, but I won’t put everything into one crop. If cotton price is only so-so or the weather turns bad, I still need some wheat and maize to steady the income and keep grain around. I’ve farmed here a long time, and in Quzhou the people who do only one thing can get hurt badly in a bad year. So this year I’ll put 8 mu in cotton, and on the other 4 mu I’ll do the usual wheat followed by summer maize.

For inputs, I won’t be too stingy, but I also won’t chase the highest rate. On my land, if wheat and maize look weak because I saved too much on fertilizer, the loss is bigger than the money saved. Still, fertilizer, water pumping, and labor all cost cash, so I’ll use moderate rates close to what has worked before. I have well irrigation, so for wheat I’ll protect the key stages, for maize I’ll give water only if summer rain is not enough, and for cotton I’ll irrigate a couple of times if the field stays dry. I’ll do most work with family labor and only hire a little help when timing gets tight.
